data.summary: Standard deviation measures spread about the mean. Use mean and SD together to compare two data sets in context.
key_concepts: Larger SD means values are more spread out / less consistent
For grouped data, use class mid-points with frequencies
Compare average (mean) and spread (SD) separately, using the question context

formulas.label: SD (ungrouped)
formulas.note: Equivalent to sqrt(mean of squares - square of mean).

formulas.label: Mean and SD (grouped)
formulas.expression: mean = sum(fx)/sum(f); s.d. = sqrt( sum(f x^2)/sum(f) - (mean)^2 )
formulas.note: x is the mid-point of each class. Write 'standard deviation' in full in answers.

worked_examples.question: Grouped marks with mid-points 55,65,75,85,95 and frequencies 15,28,18,13,8. Find mean and SD.
steps: s.d. = sqrt( mean of squares - square of mean ) ≈ 12.2 (3 s.f.)

common_mistakes.mistake: Subtracting in the wrong order inside the square root.
common_mistakes.fix: It is mean of the squares minus the square of the mean (never negative).

common_mistakes.mistake: Comparing two data sets using the mean alone.
common_mistakes.fix: Mention both the average and the spread for full marks.

exam_tips: Set out a table of mid-point x, f, fx and f x^2 before substituting.
A smaller standard deviation means more consistent results in context.
